lessons.title: Making and Receiving Phone Calls
lessons.body: When you call a business in Spanish-speaking Africa, like Equatorial Guinea or Spain, start with a clear greeting: 'Buenos dÃ­as, le habla [your name] de [your company].' If you're calling a supplier in Malabo, they may answer 'Â¿DÃ­game?' or 'Â¿AlÃ³?' â both mean 'Hello?' on the phone. Always state your purpose within the first 10 seconds. For example: 'Llamo para confirmar el pedido de 50 sacos de cemento.' Speak slowly and repeat numbers: 'El precio es 250.000 francos CFA' (in Equatorial Guinea) or '3.500 nairas' (if calling Nigeria). Write down key details: order number, quantity, price, delivery date. If you don't understand, say: 'Â¿Puede repetir mÃ¡s despacio, por favor?' or 'Â¿Puede deletrear eso?' For receiving calls, answer with your company name: 'Buenos dÃ­as, FerreterÃ­a El Progreso, Â¿en quÃ© puedo ayudarle?' Keep a pen and paper ready. Confirm every detail by repeating it back: 'Entonces, Â¿entrega el martes 15 a las 10 de la maÃ±ana?' If the line is bad, say: 'La conexiÃ³n estÃ¡ mala. Â¿Podemos hablar por WhatsApp?' In many African countries, phone credit is expensive, so keep calls under 3 minutes. End politely: 'Gracias por su tiempo. Hasta luego.' Practice with a colleague using a script. Record yourself and listen for clarity. Common phrases: 'Â¿Me escucha?' (Can you hear me?), 'No cuelgue, por favor' (Don't hang up), 'Le devuelvo la llamada' (I'll call you back). Remember, in business Spanish, use 'usted' not 'tÃº' unless you know the person well. A simple 'Â¿CÃ³mo estÃ¡?' is fine after greeting. Avoid slang. If you need to transfer, say: 'Un momento, le paso con el gerente.' Always confirm the best number to call back. This builds trust and saves money.

lessons.title: Writing a Professional Email in Spanish
lessons.body: A professional email in Spanish follows a clear structure. Start with a formal greeting: 'Estimado Sr. [Apellido]:' or 'Estimada Sra. [Apellido]:' if you know the name. If not, use 'Estimados seÃ±ores:' or 'A quien corresponda:'. In the first line, state your purpose: 'Me dirijo a usted para solicitar una cotizaciÃ³n de 200 unidades de aceite de palma.' Use 'usted' throughout. Keep paragraphs short â 2 to 3 sentences each. For example: 'Somos una empresa de distribuciÃ³n en Ghana. Necesitamos entrega en Accra antes del 30 de junio.' If you attach files, write: 'Adjunto encontrarÃ¡ nuestra lista de precios.' End with a polite closing: 'Agradezco su pronta respuesta.' Then 'Atentamente,' or 'Cordialmente,' followed by your full name, position, company, phone, and email. In Africa, email is often read on mobile phones, so use a clear subject line: 'Solicitud de cotizaciÃ³n â Pedido 1234'. Avoid long sentences. Use bullet points for lists: 'â 50 cajas de tomate â 30 kg de cebolla'. If you need a reply by a certain date, say: 'Por favor, confirme antes del viernes 10 de mayo.' For follow-ups, reply to the same email thread. If you don't get a response in 3 days, send a short reminder: 'Le escribo nuevamente para saber si recibiÃ³ mi correo anterior.' Common mistakes: using 'tÃº' instead of 'usted', forgetting accents (Ã¡, Ã©, Ã­, Ã³, Ãº), and writing in all caps. Use a professional email address like nombre@empresa.com. Sign off with 'Quedo atento a su respuesta.' Practice by drafting an email to a supplier in Spanish, then use Google Translate to check, but always verify with a fluent speaker. Save templates for common requests: quotes, orders, complaints. This saves time and reduces errors.

lessons.title: Scheduling Meetings and Appointments
lessons.body: Scheduling in Spanish requires clarity about time, date, and place. Use the 24-hour clock to avoid confusion: 'a las 15:00' means 3 PM. Days of the week: lunes, martes, miÃ©rcoles, jueves, viernes. Months: enero, febrero, marzo, etc. When proposing a meeting, say: 'Â¿Le viene bien el miÃ©rcoles 12 a las 10:00?' or 'Â¿Podemos reunirnos el prÃ³ximo lunes?' If you need to reschedule, say: 'Lo siento, no puedo el martes. Â¿Podemos cambiar al jueves?' Confirm the meeting 24 hours in advance: 'Le confirmo nuestra reuniÃ³n maÃ±ana a las 14:00 en su oficina.' In Africa, meetings may start late, but always arrive on time. For virtual meetings, specify the platform: 'Usaremos Zoom. Le enviarÃ© el enlace.' Common phrases: 'Â¿A quÃ© hora le conviene?' (What time suits you?), 'Estoy disponible el viernes por la maÃ±ana' (I'm available Friday morning), 'Â¿DÃ³nde nos reunimos?' (Where shall we meet?). If you need to cancel, do it early: 'Lamento cancelar nuestra reuniÃ³n. Â¿Podemos reprogramar para la prÃ³xima semana?' Always send a written confirmation via email or WhatsApp. For example: 'Confirmado: ReuniÃ³n el 20 de mayo a las 11:00 en la oficina de [empresa].' Use a calendar app like Google Calendar and set reminders. In business Spanish, use 'quedar' for informal appointments: 'Â¿Quedamos a las 10?' But for formal meetings, use 'reunirse'. Practice role-playing with a colleague: one proposes a time, the other accepts or suggests another. Learn to say 'No puedo, lo siento' politely. If you need to bring documents, say: 'TraerÃ© el contrato y la factura.' End with 'Gracias, nos vemos el miÃ©rcoles.' This saves time and builds professional relationships.

lessons.title: Confirming Orders and Following Up
lessons.body: Confirming orders in Spanish prevents costly mistakes. After placing an order, send a confirmation message: 'Confirmo el pedido de 100 cajas de leche a 5.000 francos CFA cada una. Total: 500.000 francos CFA. Entrega el 15 de junio.' Use numbers clearly: 'cien' (100), 'mil' (1,000), 'un millÃ³n' (1,000,000). If you need to follow up, wait 2-3 business days, then call or email: 'Llamo para confirmar si recibiÃ³ nuestro pedido.' If the supplier hasn't responded, say: 'Necesito saber si el pedido estÃ¡ en camino.' For late deliveries, be polite but firm: 'El pedido debÃ­a llegar ayer. Â¿CuÃ¡ndo llegarÃ¡?' Ask for a tracking number: 'Â¿Me puede dar el nÃºmero de seguimiento?' In Africa, follow up by WhatsApp if email fails. Use voice notes for clarity. Common phrases: 'Â¿EstÃ¡ confirmado mi pedido?' (Is my order confirmed?), 'Â¿CuÃ¡ndo sale el envÃ­o?' (When does the shipment leave?), 'Necesito la factura proforma' (I need the proforma invoice). Always keep a record: order date, quantity, price, delivery date, and any changes. If there's a problem, say: 'Faltan 10 cajas. Por favor, envÃ­enlas en el prÃ³ximo camiÃ³n.' For payment follow-up: 'Â¿Han recibido el pago?' (Have you received the payment?). If you need to change an order, do it before shipping: 'Â¿Puedo aumentar el pedido a 150 cajas?' After delivery, confirm receipt: 'RecibÃ­ el pedido completo. Gracias.' This builds trust. Practice writing a confirmation email template: 'Asunto: ConfirmaciÃ³n de pedido #1234 â Cuerpo: Estimado Sr. PÃ©rez, Confirmo el pedido de 50 sacos de arroz a 20.000 francos CFA cada uno. Total: 1.000.000 francos CFA. Entrega el 10 de julio. Gracias.' Use this for every order.

lessons.title: Using WhatsApp and Text Messaging for Business
lessons.body: WhatsApp is essential for business in Africa. Use it for quick confirmations, reminders, and sharing documents. Start with a polite greeting: 'Buenos dÃ­as, Sr. GÃ³mez. Le escribo por WhatsApp para confirmar la reuniÃ³n de maÃ±ana.' Avoid sending voice notes longer than 30 seconds â many people can't listen at work. Instead, type short messages. For orders: 'Â¿Puede enviar 20 cajas de tomate maÃ±ana?' Use emojis sparingly â a thumbs up (ð) is fine, but no smileys in formal contexts. Create a business profile with your company name and logo. Use WhatsApp Business for auto-replies: 'Gracias por su mensaje. Le responderemos en breve.' For urgent matters, call instead of texting. If you need to send a document, use PDF, not Word, to avoid formatting issues. Common phrases: 'Â¿Me confirma, por favor?' (Please confirm), 'Quedo atento' (I'll wait), 'Gracias por su respuesta.' For reminders: 'Le recuerdo nuestra cita el jueves a las 10:00.' If you don't get a reply in 2 hours, send a gentle follow-up: 'Â¿RecibiÃ³ mi mensaje anterior?' Never send messages after 8 PM or before 7 AM unless urgent. In group chats, address the person directly: '@Juan, necesito el precio.' Keep messages short: 1-2 sentences. For payment confirmations: 'Pago enviado. Por favor, confirme recepciÃ³n.' Use 'usted' for business contacts. Save contacts with company names: 'FerreterÃ­a El Progreso â Juan'. Backup chats regularly. Practice sending a professional WhatsApp: 'Buenos dÃ­as, Sra. LÃ³pez. Soy [your name] de [company]. Necesito cotizaciÃ³n de 100 kg de cafÃ©. Â¿Me puede ayudar?' This is fast, cheap, and effective.

lessons.title: Practice: Draft a Business Email to a Supplier
lessons.body: Now you will draft a complete business email in Spanish to a supplier. Follow this template. First, choose a real supplier â for example, a coffee exporter in Ethiopia or a textile manufacturer in Ghana. Write the subject line: 'Solicitud de cotizaciÃ³n â [producto]'. Then greet: 'Estimado Sr. [Apellido]:' or 'Estimados seÃ±ores:'. In the first paragraph, introduce yourself: 'Me llamo [your name] y represento a [your company] en [city, country].' State your request: 'Necesito una cotizaciÃ³n para 500 unidades de [producto].' Include specifications: size, color, quality. Ask for price, delivery time, and payment terms: 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es el precio por unidad? Â¿CuÃ¡nto tiempo tarda la entrega a [your city]? Â¿Aceptan pago contra entrega?' Mention quantity discounts: 'Â¿Ofrecen descuento por volumen?' If you need samples, ask: 'Â¿Pueden enviar una muestra?' Then close: 'Agradezco su pronta respuesta. Quedo atento a su cotizaciÃ³n.' Sign off: 'Atentamente, [your full name], [position], [company], [phone], [email].' After writing, check for accents and formal 'usted'. Use a spell checker. Then send it to yourself first to see how it looks. If you have a Spanish-speaking colleague, ask them to review. Common errors: mixing 'tÃº' and 'usted', forgetting to attach files, and writing too much. Keep it under 150 words. Practice with different scenarios: complaining about a late delivery, requesting a refund, or confirming an order. For example: 'Asunto: Reclamo por pedido #5678 â Cuerpo: Estimado Sr. Ruiz, El pedido #5678 llegÃ³ con 20 unidades faltantes. Solicito el envÃ­o inmediato de las unidades restantes o un reembolso. Gracias.' Save this template and adapt it. In Africa, email is often the first contact, so make it professional. Review your draft three times before sending.
